title: Covering-Congruence Construction for Even Integers Outside S₃

problemStatement.formal: \exists\, a, m \in \mathbb{N},\ m > 0,\quad \forall\, t \in \mathbb{N},\ (a + t m)\ \text{is even and}\ (a + t m) \notin S_3,
problemStatement.plain: The Erdős #10 thread studies which integers can be written as a prime plus a bounded number of powers of two. Using a *covering system* — a finite set of congruences whose union is all of $\mathbb{Z}$ — one can force an entire arithmetic progression to avoid such representations. The goal is to formalize that covering-congruence construction to exhibit infinitely many **even** integers that are **not** in $S_3$.

Erdos10WIP01OQ03.eq_two_pow_of_pos_of_popcount_le_one (positive popcount≤1 offset is a power of 2)
insights: Popcount reformulation of non-membership: ¬IsPrimePlusKPowers k n ↔ ∀ w≤n, popcount w≤k → ¬(n-w).Prime. Re-indexing the existing isPrimePlusKPowers_iff_popcount by the offset w=n-p. This is exactly what a covering system must control, for every k.
Even integers get the w=0 offset for free: n even and >2 is composite, so a covering construction only needs to handle POSITIVE offsets w.

At k=1 the positive offsets of popcount ≤1 are exactly the single powers 2^a; the existing prime_forced_small obstruction + parity (six covering primes are odd ⟹ 2^a odd ⟹ a=0 ⟹ n=p+1≤242) reproduces infinitely many even n ∉ S_1 natively in the IsPrimePlusKPowers predicate.

BARRIER: the elementary k=1 covering only controls single powers (q ∣ n-2^a); it says NOTHING about n-(2^a+2^b+2^c). So even-S_3 non-membership is genuinely harder (Crocker 1971 regime for k=2 and its unresolved k=3 extension), not reachable from the existing covering. The seeker tractability=5 overestimates the literal target.
sumPrimeAndTwoPows k (Erdos10Incomplete01) and IsPrimePlusKPowers k n (Erdos10OQ02) are provably equivalent (unfold: both are ∃ prime p, ∃ multiset of ≤k exponents summing to n-p).
mathlibGaps: No k=3 (or general k≥2) covering-system construction: killing every ≤3-bit offset n-(2^a+2^b+2^c) simultaneously needs a Crocker-type argument, far beyond the elementary single-power covering. Estimated multi-session / likely BLOCKED for full 0-axiom formalization.
